sourcedFrom: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup (1995)
cleanIntro: Colt's own field strip for the Series 80 Gold Cup, then the cleaning it calls for. Every step carries the manual's words and the page they sit on.

steps.title: Catch the magazine as it drops
steps.action: Put a hand under the magazine so it cannot fall, then press the magazine catch to release and eject it.
steps.prose: A target pistol's magazine is worth more than a dropped one stays worth. Catch it.
steps.quote: Place hand under magazine to prevent it from falling and press magazine catch to release and eject magazine.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 2, p.28

steps.title: Rack the chambered round out
steps.action: Using the serrated finger grips, pull the slide sharply rearward to extract and eject the round in the chamber.
steps.prose: Sharply, not gently. A slow pull is how a live round gets left sitting half out of the chamber.
steps.caution: Keep your hands clear of the ejection port to allow round to eject without obstruction.
steps.quote: Using serrated finger grips pull slide sharply rearward to extract and eject a round from the chamber.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — UNLOADING — To Unload, step 3, p.28

steps.title: Look into the chamber
steps.action: Pull the slide back slightly and look into the chamber to be sure it is empty, keeping the muzzle in a safe direction and your finger off the trigger.
steps.prose: Look — do not feel, and do not trust the extractor.
steps.quote: Pull slide back slightly and LOOK IN CHAMBER TO ENSURE
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — LOADING, step 3, p.25

steps.title: Empty the magazine as well
steps.action: Slide the remaining live rounds forward out of the magazine.
steps.prose: Forward over the feed lips, one at a time. A cleared pistol beside a loaded magazine is not a cleared pistol.
steps.quote: Remove remaining live rounds by sliding them forward out of the magazine.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — UNLOADING — To Unload, p.29

steps.title: This is the Series 80 Gold Cup procedure
steps.action: Everything below is the stripping procedure Colt publishes in its MK IV/Series 80 Gold Cup manual, the book that covers the Gold Cup National Match and the Delta Gold Cup. The Gold Cup is a Government-size .45 with a barrel bushing, a single recoil spring, a spring plug and a slide stop.
steps.prose: Two Gold Cup details matter later rather than now: the adjustable rear sight and the adjustable trigger stop, both of which Colt documents separately in Section 5.
steps.caution: Colt warns that if the trigger stop ever prevents the pistol firing, the sear could be partially engaged and the pistol could fire if jarred — release the trigger, unload immediately, and adjust the stop as described in Section 5.
steps.quote: The Colt Gold Cup National Match MK IV/Series 80 represents the ultimate in semi auto target pistols.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — SECTION 2 MAIN FEATURES, p.4

steps.title: Magazine out, pistol proven empty
steps.action: Before the strip begins, confirm again that the magazine is out and the pistol is not loaded, and be sure you have read the manual's safety instructions.
steps.prose: Colt restates the clearing at the head of its own stripping section rather than assuming you did it. Do it again anyway.
steps.quote: Ensure magazine is removed and pistol is NOT loaded.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 1, p.38

steps.title: Stand it on its butt, muzzle up
steps.action: With the muzzle pointing upward, rest the pistol on the heel of the butt and the grip safety on a table or bench.
steps.prose: This is not fussiness. The recoil spring plug is about to be released under compression, and standing the gun up puts your body out of its line.
steps.quote: With muzzle pointing upward, rest pistol on heel of butt and
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 2, p.38
steps.warn: Wear safety glasses — a spring-loaded component such as the recoil spring or plug can injure your eyes.

steps.title: Free the plug: press down and turn the bushing
steps.action: Push the slide back about a quarter inch, press down on the recoil spring plug just below the muzzle and at the same time rotate the barrel bushing clockwise about a quarter turn, using a bushing wrench if you need one.
steps.prose: Both hands are busy at once: down on the plug, round on the bushing. Let go of the plug at this point and it leaves the gun at speed.
steps.quote: Push slide back about 1/4 inch, press down on recoil spring plug (located just below muzzle) and at same time rotate barrel bushing clockwise about 1/4 turn, using barrel bushing wrench if necessary; this will free plug and recoil spring.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 3, p.39

steps.title: Let the plug and spring out under control, then part them
steps.action: Keep pressure on the plug so the spring cannot eject it, allow plug and spring to extend gradually out of the slide, then rotate the plug counterclockwise and take it off the spring.
steps.prose: Gradually is the operative word. The spring has an inch of travel it wants to use all at once.
steps.caution: Rotate plug counterclockwise and remove from spring.
steps.quote: Keep pressure on plug to prevent it being ejected by the spring, then allow plug and spring to gradually extend out of the slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, steps 3 and 4, p.39

steps.title: Cock the hammer
steps.action: Pull back on the hammer spur until the hammer is cocked.
steps.prose: The slide will not come off over a down hammer. This is the step people skip and then blame on a tight gun.
steps.quote: Cock hammer by pulling back on hammer spur.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 5, p.39

steps.title: Line up the disassembly notch and lift the slide stop out
steps.action: Pull the slide to the rear until the lug on the slide stop sits opposite the disassembly notch, push the rounded end of the slide stop pin on the right of the receiver inward and through the receiver, then lift the slide stop out.
steps.prose: The notch is a shallow half-moon in the slide rail; if the pin will not move, the notch is not lined up. Push, do not lever.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, steps 6 and 7, p.40

steps.title: Receiver off the slide
steps.action: Pull the receiver to the rear and off the slide.
steps.prose: Colt describes it as taking the frame off the slide rather than the slide off the frame — the same motion, but it is the wording in this book.
steps.quote: Pull receiver to rear and off the slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 8, p.40

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out the back of the slide
steps.action: Lift the recoil spring and its guide and draw them rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Rearward, the way they went in. A Delta Gold Cup carries two springs, one inside the other; a .45 Gold Cup has one.
steps.quote: Lift recoil spring/s and guide and pull them rearward out of slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 9, p.40

steps.title: Bushing off, then barrel out through the front
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing counterclockwise, push it forward until it is clear of the slide and remove it from the barrel, then push the barrel link forward and remove the barrel out the front of the slide.
steps.prose: The link has to be forward or the barrel lug will not clear its seat — Colt gives that its own figure for a reason.
steps.quote: Push link forward and remove barrel from front of slide.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, steps 10 and 11, p.40

steps.title: Field strip complete — and that is the limit
steps.action: Receiver, slide, barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring, spring guide, recoil spring plug, slide stop and magazine. Colt prints the bound on the next page: do not strip the pistol further, and do not remove or alter parts, particularly safety parts.
steps.prose: Anything past this line is a gunsmith's job by the manufacturer's own instruction, not a matter of confidence.
steps.quote: Do not strip your pistol further than previously described.
steps.cite: Colt MK IV/Series 80 Pistols Safety and Instruction Manual — Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — MK IV/Series 80 Pistols: Gold Cup National Match, Delta Gold Cup — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING — IMPORTANT, p.41
steps.warn: Never dry fire the pistol when the slide is removed from the receiver, and do not alter parts.

deepAbsentReason: Colt bounds this book immediately after its stripping section: "Do not strip your pistol further than previously described. Do not remove or alter parts, particularly safety parts." (p.41), and directs anything beyond it to Servicing and Repair. The only further procedures the manual publishes are trigger-stop adjustment and magazine cleaning, both of which are carried below. So this listing has NO deep clean — the manual documents no procedure past the field strip.

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Clean from the breech end forward — Colt warns that contact between cleaning rod and muzzle wears the crown and reduces accuracy, which on a target pistol is the whole point
Attach a cotton flannel patch to the rod, insert it in the breech and pass rod and patch down through the barrel, changing patches until the last one comes out clean
Inspect the bore; if it is clean skip the brush, and if it is still dirty run a brass wire bristle brush wet with gun cleaning solution the full length before reversing direction
Finish with a lightly oil-moistened patch through the bore, leaving a thin film; pass a dry patch through if the pistol is going back into use rather than storage

cleaning.name: BREECH FACE AND SLIDE
tasks: Clean the rear face of the barrel and the face of the slide with a small toothbrush
Wipe every external surface with a flannel patch lightly moistened with gun oil
Check no flannel or brush bristles have lodged anywhere in the pistol before it goes back together

cleaning.name: AFTER REASSEMBLY
tasks: Wipe the external surfaces again with an oil-moistened patch to remove fingerprints — finger moisture left behind starts corrosion
Remove gun cleaning solution and oil from the stocks

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Clean the magazine whenever the pistol is cleaned
Remove the follower and spring and clean all components, taking care to remove carbon deposits from the magazine lips and the follower
Wipe the components with a lightly oiled cloth and reassemble

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: Clean as soon after firing as possible — the job is easier and there is less chance for corrosion to start
Unfired, clean it once or twice a year in a temperate climate, or as often as once a month in a tropical one
If you carry it loaded, unload it and clean it at least once a month; if it gets wet, clean it as soon as possible
Below freezing, avoid oil and apply a dry lubricant sparingly instead

reassembly: With the slide upside down and the barrel link forward, assemble the barrel into the slide.
Place the barrel bushing over the muzzle and into the slide until it is flush with the face of the slide, then turn the bushing clockwise as far as it will go.

Place the recoil guide into the recoil spring so the closed end of the spring is against the collar of the guide — on a .45 National Match, install the lighter (green) spring for semi-wadcutter loads and the other to reduce recoil and wear with higher-pressure ammunition.
Push the open end of the spring through the slide from the rear and position the arched part of the guide over the outside of the barrel.
Cock the hammer, check the plunger lever on top of the receiver is down (forward), and tip the receiver forward to keep it down as you run the slide onto the receiver.

Look through the slide stop hole, move the slide until the hole in the barrel link lines up, insert the slide stop until it is almost home, then push the slide rearward until the disassembly notch lines up and press the slide stop fully in.

Rest the pistol muzzle up, push the slide back about a quarter inch, press the recoil spring plug down until it is fully home, and rotate the barrel bushing so its arched part straddles the plug and locks it in place.
fncheck: Colt's own post-assembly check (p.46): exercise the slide a few times by pulling it fully rearward and letting it slam forward on an empty chamber, then open and lock the slide open and look in the ejection port to be sure the firing pin is not sticking forward through the hole in the middle of the breech face. You should not be able to see it. If it is sticking forward, or the pistol discharges when you close the slide, do not use it — return it to Colt.
